17I.21 Temporal judgments are averted by humility.
22E.1 War and defeat may be brought by God as punishment for national sins.

precepts.text: If they confess their iniquity and their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they accept the punishment, then the Most High remembers his covenant; humbling brings deliverance.
precepts.point: The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

precepts.why:
“If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers … if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.”

Humbling brings deliverance. That is what happened under Rehoboam: “They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.”

“Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.” They had to learn the difference between serving the Most High and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High: accept the punishment of our iniquity, and he remembers his covenant.

precepts.text: Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem.”

So when Abijah says Rehoboam “was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them”, young and tenderhearted does not mean a small child. Rehoboam was forty and one years old when he began to reign; he simply knew nothing of war, for the land had rest in Solomon's days. That is how “vain men, the children of Belial” gathered unto Jeroboam and strengthened themselves against him.

precepts.text: When Rehoboam had established the kingdom and strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
precepts.point: Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.”

The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law. Asa did the opposite: he commanded Judah “to do the law and the commandment”, and “In his days the land was quiet ten years.”

points: When Rehoboam establishes the kingdom and strengthens himself, he forsakes the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
One who leads goes astray and carries many others with him; this is why the people must be examples to one another in righteousness, of one mind and one spirit in the rebuilding of the kingdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: In the fifth year of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem because Rehoboam transgressed against the Lord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Shishak comes with twelve hundred chariots, threescore thousand horsemen, and people without number out of Egypt, the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: He takes the fenced cities of Judah and comes to Jerusalem; the invasion is the direct result of forsaking the law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah gathered at Jerusalem and declares the word of the Lord: because they have forsaken him, he has left them in the hand of Shishak.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: The princes and the king humble themselves and say the Lord is righteous.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: When the Lord sees that they humble themselves, his word comes to Shemaiah saying he will not destroy them but grant them some deliverance, and his wrath will not be poured on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Nevertheless they will be Shishak's servants, that they may know the difference between serving the Most High and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Shishak takes away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, carrying off all the shields of gold Solomon had made.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place and commits them to the guard that keeps the entrance of the king's house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Whenever the king enters the house of the Lord the guard fetches the shields and returns them to the guard chamber.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Because Rehoboam humbles himself, the wrath of the Lord turns from him so that he is not utterly destroyed, and in Judah things go well.
Deliverance and the destruction of enemies come to the people when they humble themselves before the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns; he is forty and one years old when he begins to reign and reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord chose to put his name there.
His mother's name is Naamah an Ammonitess.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: He does evil because he prepares not his heart to seek the Lord; the failure is a heart never set on the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: The acts of Rehoboam are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies, and there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

points: Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, is buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigns in his place.
